lessonsIntro: Praa Sands is the main surf beach on Cornwall's south coast, and lessons run from the west end car park and the Stones Reef complex. It often has waves when the north coast is too big.

text: Praa Sands is a mile-long south-facing beach in Mount's Bay, and it's usually smaller than the north coast in summer. It comes into its own in autumn and winter, often working when north coast beaches are blown out or too big. Waves tend to break best around mid to high tide, close to the shore, and the quieter east end can have the better peaks.

Local guides warn that the waves can be powerful, and windsurf guides describe a heavy shore dump at high tide, so beginners should learn with a school rather than going it alone. RNLI lifeguards patrol from Easter, daily from early May to late September, and in October, with swimming and surfing areas at the busier west end. Watch out for rocky patches, especially towards the east end.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Beginners with a school
cards.text: Rated by local guides as suitable for beginners and experienced surfers, but powerful enough that a lesson is advised.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Mid to high tide, smaller days
cards.text: Waves break best around mid to high tide. Lifeguards are on daily from 2 May to 27 September in 2026.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: High-tide shore dump and rocks
cards.text: The shorebreak gets heavy near high tide, and there are rocky patches along the beach, especially at the east end.

hireIntro: You can hire kit at the west end of the beach, from the surf school in the car park or the Boatshed in the Stones Reef complex.

text: A big foam board is the safest bet on Praa Sands, where the waves break close to shore and can dump at high tide. Improvers who can handle a quick take-off can move to something shorter, especially on punchy winter days. The sea here runs from roughly 8 to 10°C in late February to 15 to 18°C around mid-August.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Foam board for learners
cards.text: Boards are included in lessons. Save harder boards for when you can make steeper, quicker take-offs.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 4/3 or 3/2 in summer, 5mm in winter
cards.text: Surf-forecast suggests a 4/3mm (or 3/2 with boots) in August, and a 5/4 or 5/3mm with gloves and boots in late February.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Bodyboards and SUP on calm days
cards.text: The Boatshed runs bodyboarding and SUP. Praa Sands has watersports zoning, so follow the flags and lifeguards' advice.

shopsIntro: Praa Sands has beach and hire shops at the west end, but we couldn't confirm a dedicated surf retail shop.
shopsText: The west end of Praa Sands has the car parks, cafes and the Stones Reef complex, where the Boatshed Activity Centre runs a year-round hire shop. Beach guides mention a surf and beach shop here, but we couldn't confirm one selling boards and wetsuits. For a full range of surf kit, Down The Line Surf Co in Hayle is the closest specialist shop we could confirm.

lessons.q: Where do surf lessons meet at Praa Sands?
lessons.a: Global Boarders meets at the Praa Sands Beach Car Park on Castle Drive, and the Boatshed Activity Centre is in the Stones Reef complex on the beach.

lessons.q: Will my lesson always be at Praa Sands?
lessons.a: Not always. Global Boarders may move lessons to Gwithian on the north coast if the waves are better there.

lessons.q: When is the best tide for surfing at Praa Sands?
lessons.a: Waves usually break best from mid to high tide, but the shorebreak can get heavy right at high tide.

hire.q: Can I hire a surfboard at Praa Sands?
hire.a: Yes, from Global Boarders at the beach car park or the Boatshed Activity Centre's hire shop.

hire.q: Is hire available out of season?
hire.a: The Boatshed describes its hire shop as running all year round, but call ahead to check.

shops.q: Is there a surf shop at Praa Sands?
shops.a: There are beach and hire shops at the west end, but no dedicated surf retailer we could confirm. Down The Line in Hayle is the closest specialist surf shop we could confirm.
